reasons.text: spec checks are a hard gate
cost delta is part of every trade-off
sells to US federal buyers: domestic content above 65%, no DoD 1260H or FCC Covered List suppliers
deploys in the US: US import duty counts, no UFLPA Entity List suppliers
deploys in Canada: Canadian duty counts
downtime is costly: lowest supply risk is an objective
parts needed within 30 days: longer lead times block
budget $1,600: a BOM over budget is a finding

data.reason: The datasheet (6-lead hybrid stepper motor from Changzhou Jingkong Motor & Electric Appliance Co., Ltd.) does not provide continuous torque, peak torque, rated speed, max speed, supply voltage, or price. It only lists holding torque (a single value per model, not continuous or peak). For a hybrid stepper motor, continuous torque is typically 50-70% of holding torque. The highest holding torque models are JK57HS112-3004 and JK57HS112-4204 at 2.8 Nm (≈394 oz-in holding), which would theoretically support the 109 oz-in continuous and 113 oz-in peak requirements, but continuous/peak torque values are not explicitly stated. Other required specs (rated speed, max speed, supply voltage, rated voltage, rated current, body length, shaft diameter, price) are also not directly available for individual models in the requested format. The document only provides resistance, inductance, detent torque, rotor inertia, and mass.
